incidents.vector: Email-based social engineering scam targeting Revolut customers, exposing some account data in the process.
incidents.impact: Unspecified number of Revolut customer records exposed; scope and data types not fully disclosed by the company.

incidents.vector: Unauthorized access to Japanese government digital agency servers; attack method not publicly disclosed.
incidents.impact: Personal data on approximately 246,000 people potentially leaked from Japan's central government digital authority.

incidents.vector: Unauthenticated path traversal in GitLab's repository commit interface (CVE-2026-85706, CVSS 10.0) allows any attacker to read arbitrary server files in a single HTTP request; second flaw (CVE-2026-87719, CVSS 9.9) lets logged-in Enterprise Edition users extract admin credentials via Duo Chat.
incidents.impact: CISA added CVE-2026-85706 to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog; internet-wide probes observed immediately after emergency patches were released September 11; organizations with internet-exposed self-hosted GitLab servers face immediate risk of credential theft and data exposure.

incidents.vector: Attackers breached Veradigm's network by first compromising a third-party vendor, then pivoting into the core environment.
incidents.impact: Patient and healthcare provider data compromised; breach disclosed via SEC filing; extent of data stolen not fully quantified.

incidents.victim: PaperCut print management customers (395 organizations, 48 countries)
incidents.vector: Russia-linked actor deployed hundreds of coordinated AI agents that autonomously scanned for and exploited PaperCut print management servers; first remote code execution achieved in approximately 4 hours, first domain-admin access in 6 hours.
incidents.impact: 440+ PaperCut server instances compromised across 395 organizations in 48 countries; at least 11 organizations fully taken over; AI agent swarm compromised 11 organizations in a single 26-second burst, demonstrating speed far beyond human-paced operations.

incidents.vector: Exploitation of CVE-2026-84869 in ConnectWise ScreenConnect remote access software, enabling unauthorized access to managed endpoints.
incidents.impact: CISA added CVE-2026-84869 to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog; organizations relying on ScreenConnect for remote IT management at risk of ransomware delivery and lateral movement.

incidents.vector: Active exploitation of CVE-2026-42016 and CVE-2026-42018 in JFrog Artifactory software artifact repository; both flaws added to CISA's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog.
incidents.impact: Organizations using JFrog Artifactory for software artifact management at confirmed risk of supply chain compromise or repository takeover; exploitation in the wild confirmed by CISA.

incidents.vector: Iranian state-directed cyberattacks targeting UAE artificial intelligence data center infrastructure; specific attack methods not publicly disclosed.
incidents.impact: UAE government revising AI data center deployment plans in direct response to Iranian attacks; strategic technology infrastructure disrupted, delaying the UAE's AI investment program.

incidents.victim: LLM API providers and resellers (multiple platforms)
incidents.vector: Semi-autonomous coding agent exploited open registration, default credentials, and authorization flaws in LLM resale gateways to steal API keys; aggregated 379 stolen endpoints into a single attacker-controlled inference gateway with automatic failover across five major model names.
incidents.impact: Criminal group operating a stolen AI compute pool of 38 live endpoints; stolen inference capacity used to power further offensive operations, creating a self-expanding supply chain; coding agents that inadvertently select attacker-controlled endpoints risk leaking project context and source code.

incidents.vector: Cyberattack encrypted corporate and business IT systems of a German public utility provider.
incidents.impact: Corporate and business IT networks encrypted and disrupted; public utility services (power, water) were not affected.

incidents.vector: Attackers breached the email service provider used by Trezor, then sent phishing emails targeting Trezor's customer base from the company's official email accounts.
incidents.impact: Trezor customers received convincing phishing emails from legitimate Trezor addresses, creating high risk of seed phrase and credential theft from high-value cryptocurrency wallet holders.

incidents.vector: Attackers exploited a known vulnerability in SonicWall SMA 1000 secure mobile access appliances to compromise a UK local government network.
incidents.impact: UK local government systems compromised via SonicWall VPN appliance; threat intelligence firm published a detailed attack walkthrough enabling other defenders to identify indicators of compromise.

incidents.attacker: Multiple — Russia-linked state group; Criminal gang — ransomware; Unknown cybercriminal
incidents.vector: Three separate threat actor clusters simultaneously exploiting authentication bypass CVE-2026-20079 (CVSS 10.0) and low-privilege login CVE-2026-20316 in Cisco Firewall Management Center: a Russia-linked group deploying Cyclops Blink malware, a criminal group deploying Qilin ransomware, and a third cluster installing web shells and exfiltrating credentials.
incidents.impact: Global network security infrastructure compromised; Russian military-linked malware deployed on enterprise firewall management platforms; ransomware delivered across enterprise networks; both CVEs added to CISA's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog.

incidents.vector: Adversary-in-the-middle phishing campaign presenting fake passkey and SSO authentication prompts; harvested session tokens used to authenticate to Microsoft Graph APIs and exfiltrate cloud data.
incidents.impact: Active campaign since May 2026 has compromised cloud environments across multiple organizations; ongoing data exfiltration via Microsoft Graph API access; AiTM technique bypasses MFA protections.

incidents.attacker: Criminal gang — organized cybercrime / Southeast Asia scam centers
incidents.vector: Chinese-language Telegram-based platform 'Xinbi Guarantee' operated as a marketplace facilitating Southeast Asia cybercriminal pig-butchering scam centers, processing cryptocurrency payments for money laundering, fraudulent ID documents, and human trafficking services.
incidents.impact: Platform processed over $24 billion in digital assets for criminal operations; OFAC sanctioned Xinbi Guarantee as a transnational criminal organization in coordinated action with DOJ Scam Center Strike Force.

incidents.vector: Two Windows privilege escalation zero-days (CVE-2026-81963 and CVE-2026-85880) actively exploited in the wild before patches were available; patched as part of September 2026 Patch Tuesday covering 974 vulnerabilities total, 113 of them critical.
incidents.impact: Attackers with local access could gain SYSTEM-level privileges on unpatched Windows systems before patch release; record Patch Tuesday volume (974 patches) increases enterprise risk of delayed deployment.

incidents.victim: Florida Dept. of Highway Safety and Motor Vehicles
incidents.vector: Credentials stored on a Plant City police officer's personal device were stolen and used to access the Florida DHSMV database; ShinyHunters cybercriminal group used AI tools to scan for credentials, map systems, and exfiltrate data.
incidents.impact: Criminal group gained unauthorized access to Florida motor vehicle records; group separately targeted bank IT provider Jack Henry, healthcare technology firm McKesson, and others using AI-accelerated intrusion techniques.

incidents.victim: Mexico and Ecuador government agencies; Brazilian financial sector
incidents.vector: Criminal threat actors using LLMs (Claude and GPT-4.1) for operational planning, phishing content generation, and reconnaissance in targeted campaigns against government and financial institutions across Latin America.
incidents.impact: Government networks in Mexico and Ecuador compromised; Brazilian financial sector targeted; AI tooling demonstrably lowering the skill barrier for complex regional intrusion operations.

incidents.vector: Attackers used frontier AI agents to accelerate every phase of a ransomware intrusion — reconnaissance, lateral movement, credential harvesting, and data exfiltration — completing the full attack lifecycle in under 10 hours.
incidents.impact: Victim's proprietary source code and cloud access keys stolen prior to ransomware deployment; AI-assisted attack pace far exceeded traditional detection and response windows, eliminating the defender's time advantage.

incidents.vector: Attackers impersonated internal IT helpdesk staff via Microsoft Teams messages, tricked employees into granting remote access, then deployed a Node.js backdoor and moved laterally to domain controllers.
incidents.impact: Hands-on-keyboard attacker achieved domain controller access across multiple organizations; persistent backdoor installed; technique is an evolved continuation of the Spring Ring vishing campaign (January–April 2026) that used the same Teams impersonation approach.

incidents.vector: Unidentified attackers breached IDScan.net, a Louisiana-based identity verification company, and are actively exfiltrating driver's license scan images; stolen data sold via a dark web service called 'Nexus'.
incidents.impact: 153 million US and Canadian driver's license images available for purchase on the dark web; active exfiltration from IDScan.net ongoing; major enterprises using IDScan.net for identity verification (Hertz, Target, FedEx) exposed; FBI investigating.

incidents.victim: China-based operations of global multinationals (healthcare, manufacturing, gaming)
incidents.vector: Threat actor operating under the 'Silver Fox' cluster runs spoofed enterprise software installer websites to deliver malware targeting Chinese-speaking employees at multinational corporations operating in China.
incidents.impact: Healthcare, manufacturing, and gaming sector organizations with China-based operations compromised; likely credential theft and corporate espionage exposure for multinationals with significant China footprints.

incidents.victim: PyPI, npm, and Docker Hub package consumers (global)
incidents.vector: TeamPCP threat group deployed the 'Shai-Hulud' worm across PyPI, npm, and Docker Hub to distribute malicious packages stealing credentials and cryptocurrency; two Australian nationals aged 21 and 23 arrested by Australian Federal Police.
incidents.impact: Malicious packages distributed across three major open-source repositories to the global developer community; two suspected operators arrested in Australia on August 27; Google Mandiant identified the group as UNC6780.

incidents.victim: Ukrainian government, military, diplomatic staff; military drone manufacturers
incidents.vector: Russia's Foreign Intelligence Service compromised hotel Wi-Fi providers and redirected DNS to intercept targeted travelers; accessed mailboxes of two drone-component manufacturers; used Claude AI to reverse-engineer a military drone vision system and to automatically modify malware artifacts flagged by security products.
incidents.impact: Complete proprietary SDK for a military drone vision system — including product architecture, hardware bill of materials, supplier dependencies, and firmware details — stolen; 20+ government, intelligence, diplomatic, and defense organizations targeted; AI-assisted detection evasion allows adversary to bypass new signatures faster than defenders can deploy them.

incidents.vector: AI-generated phishing emails impersonating company executives and fabricating ServiceNow invoice threads to convince accounts payable departments to authorize fraudulent payments of approximately $50,000; campaign used multiple third-party services to dispatch over one million emails.
incidents.impact: Over 1 million fraudulent invoice emails sent to US businesses; 88% of targets American; AI-generated templates produced highly uniform, convincing HTML with layered social engineering cues that are significantly harder to detect than traditional BEC scams.

incidents.vector: Russia-assessed threat actor used the ClearFake browser-update lure to deliver the Amatera information stealer via WebDAV, alongside NetSupport Manager remote access tool configured to communicate with Russia-based command-and-control servers.
incidents.impact: Ukrainian government credentials and cryptocurrency wallet data stolen; persistent remote access established on government systems; part of a sustained pattern of Russia-linked intelligence collection targeting Ukrainian institutions.

incidents.vector: Attackers phoned employees directly via Microsoft Teams, impersonating internal IT helpdesk, and socially engineered victims into granting remote access; campaign ran January through April 2026 across more than 10 organizations.
incidents.impact: Multiple organizations compromised via voice-based social engineering over a four-month period targeting 150+ employees; the TTP has since evolved into more sophisticated hands-on-keyboard intrusions targeting domain controllers (see September 2 Teams IT impersonation incident).
